cues.en: So we're here today to talk to you about one of our favorite topics, ZFS.
cues.zh: 今天我们来聊聊我们最喜欢的话题之一：ZFS。

cues.en: So give you a little overview of what ZFS is, what the heck were we thinking anyway for those of you who haven't had time to look at it much.
cues.zh: 先简单概述一下 ZFS 是什么，以及我们当初到底是怎么想的，尤其给那些还没时间深入了解的人。

cues.en: So one of the biggest concepts we really wanted to introduce in ZFS was the concept of pooled storage.
cues.zh: 我们在 ZFS 中最想引入的核心概念之一，就是池化存储。

cues.en: That is
cues.zh: 也就是说

cues.en: get rid of the notion that a file system is tied to a unit of physical storage, whether it be a disk or a volume or whatever.
cues.zh: 摆脱文件系统必须绑定到某个物理存储单元的观念，不管那是一块磁盘、一个卷还是别的什么。

cues.en: We wanted it to operate more like what a virtual memory system does for memory. That is when you want to add more memory to your server, what do you do? Well, theoretically you power it down first, plug in more DIMMs, turn it on, poof you're done. You don't run DIMM config or create virtual DIMMs or mount them on applications
cues.zh: 我们希望它的运作方式更像虚拟内存系统管理内存那样。也就是说，当你想给服务器加内存时，你会怎么做？理论上，先关机，插上更多 DIMM，再开机，砰，搞定。你不需要运行 DIMM 配置，也不需要创建虚拟 DIMM，再把它们挂到应用上

cues.en: or anything like that. It's just everything gets better. It's all automatic. It's a resource that's managed by the operating system on behalf of applications.
cues.zh: 或者做任何类似的事。一切就是变得更好。全都是自动的。它是操作系统代表应用管理的一种资源。

cues.en: Application needs more memory, calls malloc, it's done using it, calls free.
cues.zh: 应用需要更多内存，就调用 malloc；用完了，就调用 free。

cues.en: That's all there is. And in the meantime it has a little token, a virtual address that it gives to the operating system to reference the data that it's storing. So why can't storage be the same way? More automatic, less user twiddling and just let the computers do what they're good at which is managing resources and doing all the grunt work.
cues.zh: 就这么简单。与此同时，它有个小小的凭据，一个虚拟地址，交给操作系统来引用它正在存储的数据。那存储为什么不能也这样？更自动化，少让用户瞎折腾，让计算机去做它们擅长的事——管理资源、干完所有苦活累活。

cues.en: So the other thing we really wanted to introduce was we
cues.zh: 所以我们非常想引入的另一件事是，我们

cues.en: wanted to have things always be consistent. The database guys have been doing this for literally decades
cues.zh: 希望数据能始终保持一致。做数据库的那帮人做这个都做了几十年了，

cues.en: and seem to be doing a pretty good job at it. So we really wanted the core of ZFS, the guts in the middle to be a transactional object system.
cues.zh: 而且干得相当不错。所以我们真心希望 ZFS 的核心，也就是它最深处的内核，是一个事务性对象系统。

cues.en: So everything is always consistent on disk. It doesn't matter what kind of data you're storing in there, whether it's file,
cues.zh: 这样磁盘上的所有数据就始终是一致的。不管你在里面存什么样的数据，无论是文件、

cues.en: block, swap, route, whatever, it's just at its heart, it's a transactional object.
cues.zh: 块、swap、路由还是别的什么，它的本质就是一个事务性对象。

cues.en: The third thing was we really wanted to make a reliable storage system by having provable end to end data integrity.
cues.zh: 第三点是，我们非常想通过可证明的端到端数据完整性，打造一个可靠的存储系统。

cues.en: That is, create a signature of the data when the application generates it, and then later when the application consumes it, validate that it's still the same data.
cues.zh: 也就是说，在应用生成数据时创建数据签名，之后应用消费它时，再验证它是否还是原来的数据。

cues.en: So historically,
cues.zh: 在过去，

cues.en: people have said, you can't do that. Making a pass over the data, evil, evil,
cues.zh: 大家总会说：你不能那么做。把数据完整遍历一遍？太不可思议了，大逆不道，

cues.en: just don't.
cues.zh: 千万别这么干。

cues.en: However, a lot of things have changed since people last seriously investigated this problem.
cues.zh: 然而，自从人们上次认真研究这个问题以来，情况已经发生了很大变化。

cues.en: That is
cues.zh: 那就是，

cues.en: everything in compute has gotten faster. CPUs are about a thousand times faster, memory is about a 100 times faster, and disk is about 10x faster than it was say ten, fifteen years ago.
cues.zh: 计算领域的一切都变快了。相比十到十五年前，CPU 快了大约一千倍，内存快了大约一百倍，而磁盘只快了大约十倍。

cues.en: So while everything's faster, the ratios of these speeds has changed somewhat dramatically.
cues.zh: 所以虽然一切都变快了，但它们之间的速度比率却发生了巨大的变化。

cues.en: So what that means is that before the idea, you know, back in the early nineties of making a pass over data while it streams in from your IO subsystem and out the network was a
cues.zh: 这意味着，在九十年代初，当数据从 IO 子系统流入并流出到网络时对它遍历一遍的想法，简直就是一个

cues.en: syntax error. Can't do that.
cues.zh: “语法错误”。根本行不通。

cues.en: But now what we found is that making a pass over the data can happen at speeds that are, you know, saturating the memory bus. So multiple gigabytes a second per core.
cues.zh: 但现在我们发现，遍历数据的速度非常快，甚至可以说是跑满了内存总线。单核每秒就能处理好几个 GB。

cues.en: So either you have one heck of an IO subsystem to keep up with that several giga second that a single core can
cues.zh: 所以，要么你得有一个超级强悍的 IO 子系统，才能跟上单核每秒好几个 G 的

cues.en: validate
cues.zh: 验证速度，

cues.en: or
cues.zh: 要么——

cues.en: much more likely use a fraction of a CPU to validate, you know, the hundreds of megs a second that's flowing through your system.
cues.zh: 更有可能的是——只用一小部分 CPU 性能，去处理你系统中每秒流过的几百兆数据。

cues.en: And lastly,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: because people's storage systems are growing ever bigger. People don't say, wow, look, a terabyte disk. Great. I just have to buy one for my data center.
cues.zh: 因为人们的存储系统越来越大。大家不会说：哇，快看，有个 1TB 的硬盘。太棒了，我给数据中心买一个就行。

cues.en: Nope. People buy more disks and they get ever bigger and that's a lot of storage to manage.
cues.zh: 才不是。人们会买更多、容量更大的硬盘，需要管理的存储实在是太多了。

cues.en: So why not let the computer help you out and provide
cues.zh: 所以，为什么不让计算机来帮帮忙，提供

cues.en: just simple administration,
cues.zh: 简单的管理，

cues.en: concisely express your intent and let the file system and or ZFS
cues.zh: 简洁地表达你的意图，然后让文件系统，或者特别是

cues.en: in particular
cues.zh: ZFS

cues.en: handle all the details of getting that work done. But Bill, I thought that storage was a solved problem.
cues.zh: 来处理所有底层细节呢？但是，Bill，我以为存储已经是一个被解决的问题了。

cues.en: Surely,
cues.zh: 当然啦，

cues.en: all the things that exist in storage today are happy and wonderful. Could you give me examples of what's wrong with storage today?
cues.zh: 现在存储领域的所有东西都挺好、挺美妙的。你能举例说说现在的存储有什么问题吗？

cues.en: You know, can't think of a single thing.
cues.zh: 你知道的，我简直想不出有什么问题。

cues.en: Oh, these. Yes, that's right. Boy.
cues.zh: 哦，这些。对，没错。天哪。

cues.en: So some trouble with existing file systems and they're not listed in any particular order.
cues.zh: 现有文件系统确实存在一些麻烦，它们的列出顺序不分先后。

cues.en: But number one is that there's really no defense against silent data corruption.
cues.zh: 但第一点是，真的无法防御静默数据损坏。

cues.en: Anything that happens to your data anywhere along the path can potentially cause you problems.
cues.zh: 任何沿着传输路径发生在你的数据身上的事，都可能会给你带来麻烦。

cues.en: And you know, people say, well, how often does that really happen anyway? Well, it happens often enough that people notice.
cues.zh: 你知道，人们会说，这到底能有多经常发生呢？其实它发生的频率已经足够让人注意到了。

cues.en: Noisy data corruption, which is where you know, do an IO to a driver, a storage array,
cues.zh: 有噪声的数据损坏，也就是你知道的，对驱动程序或存储阵列进行 I/O 操作，

cues.en: twiddle your thumbs for a while and it comes back and says, you know, gee, sorry pal, couldn't get that data for you and here's why. Everybody in the world knows how to deal with that. Any volume manager, any file system, when the storage subsystem is polite enough to tell you it couldn't do what you asked it to, yeah, easy to deal with. What's very difficult to deal with traditionally
cues.zh: 空等了一会儿后它返回并对你说，嘿，抱歉伙计，没能为你取回数据，原因如下。世上每个人都知道该怎么处理这种事。任何卷管理器、任何文件系统，当存储子系统足够礼貌地告诉你它无法完成你要求的事时，是的，这很好处理。而传统上非常难以处理的

cues.en: is the idea that you give the
cues.zh: 情况是，你向

cues.en: IO subsystem a request and it comes back and says, here's some data.
cues.zh: I/O 子系统发送了一个请求，它返回并说，给你一些数据。

cues.en: And really wasn't the data you were looking for. That is a lot harder to deal with.
cues.zh: 而这根本不是你要找的数据。这就难处理得多了。

cues.en: And as a person from one of the world's largest drive vendors once told me, there are two kinds of discs in the world. Those that have failed and those that are about to fail. And you know, experience has sort of proven that one out.
cues.zh: 正如全球最大硬盘供应商之一的一位代表曾经对我说的那样，世上有两种磁盘：一种是已经坏了的，另一种是即将坏的。你知道，经验已经在某种程度上证明了这一点。

cues.en: The second thing is that when you're talking about petabytes of data,
cues.zh: 第二点是，当你在谈论PB级别的数据时，

cues.en: how much of your time do you think you're going to spend managing that? Probably far more than you would like. So it's really brutal to manage things of that kind of scale.
cues.zh: 你觉得你会花多少时间来管理它们？可能远比你希望的要多。因此，管理这种规模的东西简直是一场灾难。

cues.en: First
cues.zh: 首先，

cues.en: of all, introduce some new storage in there. What's the first thing you got to do? Label the disk, partition it,
cues.zh: 要在这里引入一些新的存储。你得先做什么？给磁盘打标签、分区，

cues.en: grind them up into volumes and provision them. How much is this file system going to need? How much is that file system going to need two years from now? I don't know. I just want to have enough storage.
cues.zh: 把它们划分成卷并配置好。这个文件系统需要多大容量？两年后那个文件系统又需要多大？我不知道。我只想要足够的存储空间。

cues.en: And edit
cues.zh: 然后编辑

cues.en: your favorite files in the operating system to make sure that they're remembered.
cues.zh: 操作系统中你常用的那些文件，确保它们能被记住。

cues.en: And what do you get in return for all this work that you just did? Oh, you get lots of limits. Just what you wanted. You can only have so big a file system. Files are limited to particular size.
cues.zh: 你做了这么多工作，换来的是什么？哦，你得到了一大堆限制。正是你想要的。文件系统最大只能这么大。文件大小被限制在特定值。

cues.en: You only have so many inodes. You only have so many files per directory, things like that or number of snapshots in some cases.
cues.zh: inode 数量有限。每个目录下的文件数量有限，诸如此类，某些情况下快照数量也有限。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: there's different tools to manage different kinds of data. There's one for managing files, one for managing block storage, one for iSCSI,
cues.zh: 管理不同种类的数据要用不同的工具。一个管文件，一个管块存储，一个管 iSCSI，

cues.en: one for NFS, one for SIFs. What a pain.
cues.zh: 一个管 NFS，一个管 SIFs。真是麻烦。

cues.en: And then again, most things aren't portable between platforms. I create a file system on x86, I want to take it over to my PowerPC or Sparkbox.
cues.zh: 再者，大多数东西在不同平台之间不可移植。我在 x86 上创建了一个文件系统，想拿到我的 PowerPC 或 Spark 机器上用。

cues.en: Yeah, we're sorry about that. Or if it is portable,
cues.zh: 是啊，对此我们很抱歉。或者就算它可移植，

cues.en: usually what they do is like an EXT3 they say, everything on disk, little Indian. So if you're on a big Indian system, hope you like byte swapping. Similarly like Veritas, it's all big Indian. So if you run it on a little Indian system, same thing. Byte swapping all day.
cues.zh: 通常它们的做法是，比如 EXT3，他们说磁盘上一切都是大端序。所以如果你在大端序系统上，那就祈祷你喜欢字节交换吧。类似地，Veritas 也全是大端序。所以如果你在小端序系统上运行它，同样的事。整天字节交换。

cues.en: And lastly, because of the way a lot of these were designed, things tend to be slow.
cues.zh: 最后，由于很多这类系统的设计方式，性能往往很慢。

cues.en: Back when you know you had a 100 meg file system and you're only going to have a few thousand files,
cues.zh: 回想当年，你只有一个 100 兆的文件系统，而且只打算存几千个文件，

cues.en: literally scanning a directory to find the entry you want, what's
cues.zh: 直接扫描目录来找你想要的条目，有什么

cues.en: the big deal? Now if you have, as some of our customers do, literally hundreds of millions of files in the same directory because it's really a directory full of hashes.
cues.zh: 大不了的？但现在，就像我们一些客户那样，同一个目录里实实在在有上亿个文件，因为这个目录里装满了哈希值。

cues.en: Well, now that linear scan
cues.zh: 那么现在，这种线性扫描

cues.en: is going to cost you a little bit more.
cues.zh: 的成本就会高一些了。

cues.en: And similarly,
cues.zh: 同样地，

cues.en: fine grain locking, no, usually not there. You get fixed block sizes,
cues.zh: 细粒度锁，通常是没有的。你得到的是固定块大小，

cues.en: all sorts of painful things that have just grown up historically over time.
cues.zh: 以及各种随着时间历史积累下来的痛苦问题。

cues.en: So what are we really trying to do? Really just trying to end the suffering, you know, figure out why has storage gotten so complicated because, you know, people aren't dumb. They do things for a very good reason.
cues.zh: 那我们到底想做什么？其实就是想终结这种折磨，弄清楚为什么存储变得这么复杂，因为人们并不笨。他们做事都有很好的理由。

cues.en: But ten years from now, does that reason still exist? Well, probably not. Computing has taught us one thing, is that
cues.zh: 但十年之后，那个理由还在吗？大概不在了。计算教会我们一件事，那就是

cues.en: change is a rather frighteningly fast and constant thing.
cues.zh: 变化快得吓人，而且从不停止。

cues.en: So when you actually dig down to what are the fundamental laws of physics in solving this problem, turns out that there are a lot of obsolete assumptions you encounter along the way. So what we decided to do is to design an integrated system from scratch, handling everything from, you know, the application down to the storage and back again.
cues.zh: 所以当你真正深入探究解决这个问题的基本物理定律时，会发现沿途有很多过时的假设。于是我们决定从零开始设计一个集成系统，处理从应用层一直到存储层再返回的所有事情。

cues.en: You know, literally start with a screen full of Tildes, you know, VI is your editor, and off you go. Sort of a... Of course, VI is your editor.
cues.zh: 你知道的，字面上讲，一开机满屏幕都是波浪号，VI 就是你的编辑器，然后就开始了。某种程度上……当然啦，VI 就是你的编辑器。

cues.en: Well, you never know.
cues.zh: 嗯，这可说不准。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以呢，

cues.en: of course, you've probably heard Andrew Morgan famously has called ZFS a rampant layering violation.
cues.zh: 当然啦，你大概听说过，Andrew Morgan 曾直言不讳地称 ZFS 是一种无节制的层级违背。

cues.en: And we take a somewhat different view, of course, which is that actually the layers that exist in the storage subsystems today are actually part of the problem.
cues.zh: 当然，我们的看法有些不同，事实上，现今存储子系统里存在的各种层级，其实正是问题的一部分。

cues.en: And it's useful to go back in time and ask ourselves, why do volumes drift? Why are things structured this way? And if you think about it, going back to the late eighties when this technology started to to come into existence, it it was all the same time frame as Patterson's rate paper and people started to exceed the capacity limits of individual disk drives.
cues.zh: 回溯过去并自问一下是很有用的：为什么卷会漂移？为什么事情会这样构建？如果你仔细想想，回到八年代末这项技术开始萌芽的时候，那和 Patterson 的 RAID 论文几乎是同一时期，人们开始突破单个磁盘驱动器的容量限制。

cues.en: And originally, the idea was that
cues.zh: 而最初的想法是，

cues.en: there was a... If you go back even before that,
cues.zh: 这里有一个……如果你再往回追溯一下，

cues.en: that a disk was comparably speaking a large thing. There's a lot of storage on there. In fact, first thing you do with the disk is slice it up into partitions and then you would have a file system managing each partition. But as people's needs for data grew,
cues.zh: 相对而言，以前的磁盘是个大物件。上面有很大的存储空间。事实上，拿到磁盘你做的第一件事就是把它切成各个分区，然后用一个文件系统去管理每个分区。但随着人们对数据需求的长足增长，

cues.en: they wanted to have the ability to do a number of things. They have either more storage capacity in the form of multiple discs or
cues.zh: 他们希望能够实现好几件事情。他们要么需要由多块磁盘组成的更大存储容量，

cues.en: redundancy for the data so you can tolerate drive failure, so Yaramino Ray.
cues.zh: 要么需要数据的冗余，以便能容忍驱动器的故障，也就是 RAID。

cues.en: And then improve bandwidth
cues.zh: 然后通过将数据条带化分布在多个驱动器上

cues.en: in the form of having multiple drives across which the data gets striped. The nice thing is you can provide all of those capabilities
cues.zh: 来提高带宽。好处在于你可以提供所有这些功能

cues.en: without changing the interface between the file system and the block device. All you do is insert this little shin layer that ended up being called a volume that speaks the block device protocol out the top and the block device protocol at the bottom,
cues.zh: 而无需更改文件系统和块设备之间的接口。你所做的只是插入这个被称为卷的小巧胶水层，它在顶部和底部都使用块设备协议进行通信，

cues.en: and because of that, it inserts compatibility in between any file system and any storage system.
cues.zh: 正因如此，它在任意文件系统和任意存储系统之间建立了兼容性。

cues.en: And the nice thing about this is it's fairly easy to write one. Right? And in fact, you can even picture if you've never done it before, you can you can picture in your mind what the code looks like for, say,
cues.zh: 这样做的好处是编写这样一个东西相当容易。对吧？事实上，如果你以前没写过，你甚至可以在脑海中想象出它的代码是什么样子的，比如

cues.en: concatenation
cues.zh: 拼接

cues.en: of two
cues.zh: 两个

cues.en: one terabyte drives. Right? You wanna create a two terabyte volume, so the offset comes in, if it's less than a terabyte, you send it to this drive, if it's greater than a terabyte, you subtract one terabyte, send it to that drive. That's it. It's a fairly simple thing. So the good news about the file system volume manager architecture
cues.zh: 一太字节的驱动器。对吧？你想创建一个两太字节的卷，当偏移量进来时，如果小于一太字节，你就把它发给这个驱动器；如果大于一太字节，你就减去一太字节，然后发给那个驱动器。就是这样。这是一件相当简单的事情。所以文件系统卷管理器架构的好消息是

cues.en: is that you didn't have to change the existing software for it to work.
cues.zh: 你不需要修改现有的软件就能让它工作。

cues.en: The bad thing though is that inherent limitations in that interface are really impossible to fix without tearing it up.
cues.zh: 不过坏处在于，如果不把它推倒重来，该接口中固有的局限性实际上是无法解决的。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: by way of analogy,
cues.zh: 打个比方，

cues.en: it's useful to think about what is the abstraction
cues.zh: 思考一下卷管理器提供的

cues.en: that a volume manager provides. Well, really what it's giving you is a virtual disk. Right? Because a volume, as I say, speaks to block device protocol at the top, so it looks like a disk drive to every file system that wants to speak to it. And that means that you can plug it under a file system, it's all compatible.
cues.zh: 抽象是什么会很有帮助。嗯，它真正给你的其实是一个虚拟磁盘。对吧？因为如我所说，卷在顶部使用块设备协议，所以对于任何想要与它通信的文件系统来说，它看起来就像一个磁盘驱动器。这意味着你可以把它插在文件系统下面，并且完全兼容。

cues.en: But it means that all the hassles that you're accustomed to, partitioning for each file system, growing and shrinking as a manual process, you know,
cues.zh: 但这意味着那些你习以为常的繁琐操作，比如给每个文件系统划分分区，手动扩容和缩容，

cues.en: limited bandwidth, you know, you can see in this picture,
cues.zh: 受限的带宽等等。你看这张图，

cues.en: we've got a file system volume manager,
cues.zh: 我们有一个文件系统卷管理器，

cues.en: and say, pair of mirror drives.
cues.zh: 比方说，还有一对镜像盘。

cues.en: And that's great if what you want is completely partitioned
cues.zh: 如果你想要的是完全隔离的

cues.en: access to the data, but if it's... As is more typical, there are times when, say, the file system on the left is very busy and these two are not so much. What we really like is the ability to have the bandwidth of all those drives available to you, not just the bandwidth of this one pair. Same thing for capacity. We like the ability to say, if one file system needs to grow relative to the others, it should have access to that capacity.
cues.zh: 数据访问，那挺好的，但要是……更常见的情况是，有时左边的文件系统非常繁忙，而这两个却没那么忙。我们真正想要的是能够利用所有这些硬盘的带宽，而不仅仅是这一对的带宽。容量方面也是同理。我们希望如果某个文件系统需要比其他文件系统扩展得更大，它就能使用那些容量。

cues.en: So the extraction that we adopted with ZFS in the pooled storage model is much more like what you have in a virtual memory system with the mallet free model. Right? You don't create applications with a fixed quantity
cues.zh: 所以我们在 ZFS 存储池模型中采用的抽象，其实更像是虚拟内存系统中的 malloc/free 模型。对吧？你不会给应用程序分配固定大小

cues.en: of memory and then administratively
cues.zh: 的内存，然后通过运维手段去手动

cues.en: manipulate them. You create them with an essentially infinite address space, and then you populate that just on demand. So it's really like a malloc free abstraction in which the storage pool is like the page pool of the VM system.
cues.zh: 调整它们。你创建它们时给的是一个本质上无限的地址空间，然后按需分配填充。所以这非常像 malloc/free 抽象，其中存储池就像虚拟内存系统的页面池。

cues.en: Each instance of a file system is like an application and it simply consumes from the storage pool as it needs things. So when you create a file in ZFS,
cues.zh: 每个文件系统实例就像一个应用程序，仅在需要时从存储池中消耗资源。因此，当你在 ZFS 中创建文件时，

cues.en: that causes blocks to be allocated from the storage pool. When you remove a file, that causes the blocks to be given back to the storage pool.
cues.zh: 就会触发从存储池中分配数据块。当你删除文件时，这些数据块就会被归还给存储池。

cues.en: So the concept of how much free space do you have in a file system
cues.zh: 所以文件系统里到底还有多少可用空间这个概念

cues.en: doesn't even really make sense anymore. It... The file stream consumes exactly as much space as
cues.zh: 已经完全没有意义了。它……文件流消耗的空间

cues.en: the data that it represents, no more, no less.
cues.zh: 精确等于它所代表的数据大小，不多也不少。

cues.en: Just as an application,
cues.zh: 就像作为一个应用程序，

cues.en: you can talk about the size that it's consuming,
cues.zh: 你可以讨论它正在消耗的大小，

cues.en: but you would never ask how much free memory does Firefox have? I like a zero. Yeah.
cues.zh: 但你绝不会问 Firefox 有多少可用内存？我喜欢零。没错。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: the concept of an application having free memory doesn't make sense. The VM system is fundamentally global to all applications.
cues.zh: 应用程序拥有可用内存这个概念是没有意义的。虚拟机系统从根本上对所有应用程序都是全局的。

cues.en: And this gives you a bunch of nice things. There's no need to manage partitions because you're just taking all the storage and pulling it.
cues.zh: 这会带来许多好处。无需管理分区，因为你只是把所有的存储都拿来汇聚在一起。

cues.en: The grow and shrink are not... I say automatically here, but it's not even really automatic as much as it's implicit.
cues.zh: 增长和收缩不是……我这里说的是自动，但与其说是自动，不如说它是隐式的。

cues.en: It's just as you put load in the files, things come and go, and there is no administrative operation corresponding to that.
cues.zh: 就像你往文件里加载数据一样，数据来来去去，没有任何与之对应的管理操作。

cues.en: You clearly have all the bandwidth. You can see from the basic idea when you come in with a bunch of rights and they hit the storage pool, we just strike those dynamically across
cues.zh: 你显然拥有全部带宽。从基本思路就能看出，当你发起大量写入操作它们击中存储池时，我们会将这些写入动态地分散到

cues.en: however many drives we've got available. And since the storage
cues.zh: 我们拥有的任意数量的可用驱动器上。而且由于存储

cues.en: is shared, there are no
cues.zh: 是共享的，所以

cues.en: partitions to manage in terms of there's this much space for one, that much space for another. It's all dynamic.
cues.zh: 无需管理诸如“这个给多少空间，那个给多少空间”这样的分区。这一切都是动态的。

cues.en: So looking at the interfaces Jeff was talking about a second ago is
cues.zh: 因此，看看 Jeff 刚才谈到的那些接口，

cues.en: the traditional file system volume manager stack as he mentioned was the block device interface on top, the block device interface on the bottom.
cues.zh: 正如他所提到的，传统的文件系统卷管理器栈的顶部和底部都是块设备接口。

cues.en: And it's pretty straightforward,
cues.zh: 而且非常直观，

cues.en: semantically
cues.zh: 从语义上讲

cues.en: poor,
cues.zh: 很贫乏，

cues.en: perfectly adequate interface
cues.zh: 但接口极其够用，

cues.en: which is write this block, read this block.
cues.zh: 也就是写这个块，读那个块。

cues.en: Yay, there you go, read and write.
cues.zh: 太棒了，就是这样，读和写。

cues.en: And what this means is that
cues.zh: 这意味着

cues.en: in the early days, loss of power meant loss of on disc consistency.
cues.zh: 在早期，断电就意味着磁盘上的数据失去一致性。

cues.en: And people scratched their heads at this for a while and said, well,
cues.zh: 人们对此苦思冥想了一阵子，然后说，好吧，

cues.en: we'll just clean it up with FSCK. Then they said, well, you know, really I don't like waiting for FSCK so let's add journaling.
cues.zh: 我们用 FSCK 清理一下就行。接着他们又说，你知道的，其实我不想等 FSCK 运行完，所以我们加个日志吧。

cues.en: So before I write something to this, let me scribble on a little post it note, you know, note to self. I was removing this file. So that if you lose power, then when you come back up, you read this say, what the heck was... Oh yeah, I was, you know, erasing this file. So that way it's sort of a targeted FSCK I guess you can think of it as.
cues.zh: 所以在往这写入之前，让我先在小便签上乱涂乱画一下，给自己留个条。我刚才在删这个文件。这样如果断电了，等你重新启动时，读一下就会说，刚才到底……哦对，我刚才在擦除这个文件。所以这有点像是有针对性的 FSCK，你可以这么理解。

cues.en: And that's how you maintain on disk consistency.
cues.zh: 这就是你维护磁盘一致性的方式。

cues.en: So the file system is off doing what it's sold,
cues.zh: 因此，文件系统在做它份内的事，

cues.en: doing a whole bunch of reads and writes to what it thinks of as a disk, which is really the volume manager. And the volume manager is like, wonder what's going on. All I see are these reads and writes, I guess I really have no idea. So better just do as I'm told. So, you know, if the volume manager is providing a mirror,
cues.zh: 对它认为的磁盘（其实是卷管理器）执行大量的读写操作。而卷管理器则想，到底怎么回事。我看到的只有这些读写，我其实完全不知道。所以还是照着吩咐做吧。因此，如果卷管理器提供了一个镜像，

cues.en: write each block to each side to keep the mirrors in sync. You lose power. Oh, guess it's time to resync. Which side of the mirror is the right one?
cues.zh: 就把每个块写入两侧，以保持镜像同步。断电了。哦，看来该重新同步了。镜像的哪一侧才是对的呢？

cues.en: I don't know. How about the left one?
cues.zh: 我也不知道。要不选左边那个？

cues.en: And you know all this is synchronous. Of course just like the file system guys started doing journaling to help with this problem, you know the volume managers do dirty region logging or use NVRAM or some other things such that they keep a little bit of state off to the side. So Rather than syncing the entire devices back together, they just do the parts that were in flight at the time. But again, sort of a
cues.zh: 而且大家知道这些全是同步的。当然，就像做文件系统的团队引入日志技术来解决这个问题一样，卷管理器也会做脏区域日志，或者使用 NVRAM 之类的方式在旁边维护一点状态。这样就不用重新把整个设备完全同步一遍，只需同步当时正在写入的部分。但这依然有点像……

cues.en: flip a coin sort of thing in terms of which side of the mirror has your data on it? I don't know. Wish I could tell you. So in ZFS we factored the problem a little bit differently. So
cues.zh: 有点像抛硬币：镜像的哪一侧才有你的真实数据？我不知道，我也希望能告诉你。所以在 ZFS 中，我们对这个问题的拆解方式有所不同。所以

cues.en: rampant layering violation comments aside,
cues.zh: 暂且抛开那些关于“严重违背分层架构”的吐槽，

cues.en: what we decided to do is say the core
cues.zh: 我们的做法是，认定核心的

cues.en: function, sort of the workhorse of ZFS is what's called the DMU, the data management unit. Sort of mentally in our minds at least, analogous to the virtual memory or the memory management unit in
cues.zh: 功能，也就是 ZFS 的核心主力模块，是所谓的 DMU（数据管理单元）。至少在我们脑海中，它类似于

cues.en: a CPU.
cues.zh: CPU 里的虚拟内存或内存管理单元。

cues.en: So what the DMU does is it doesn't know what a file is, doesn't know what a directory is. All it knows is that there are objects and transactions on those objects.
cues.zh: DMU 的特点在于，它根本不知道什么是文件，也不知道什么是目录。它只知道存在对象，以及作用在这些对象上的事务。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 并且

cues.en: it provides that sort of an interface up to what we call the ZPL or the ZFS POSIX layer. And what the POSIX layer does, it has all your favorite system calls coming in the top, open, close, read, write, rename, unlink,
cues.zh: 它把这种接口向上提供给所谓的 ZPL，也就是 ZFS POSIX 层。而 POSIX 层的作用，就是在顶层承接大家最常用的各种系统调用：open、close、read、write、rename、unlink，

cues.en: c times or u times.
cues.zh: 以及 ctime 或 utime。

cues.en: And it takes those and translates them into transactions on objects. So that given the transactional object store, you could imagine writing the ZPL isn't quite the onerous task it might otherwise be. So for example, a rename system call comes in and says, rename this file from this directory to that directory.
cues.zh: 它接收这些操作，并把它们转换成对象上的事务。因此，有了这个事务型对象存储，你可以想象，编写 ZPL 并不像原本可能那样是一项繁重的任务。比如，来了一个 rename 系统调用，说：把这个文件从这个目录重命名到那个目录。

cues.en: So what the ZPL does is, I know just how to do this. I'll create a transaction and as part of this transaction,
cues.zh: 所以 ZPL 做的是：我知道该怎么做。我会创建一个事务，并作为这个事务的一部分，

cues.en: I want to modify the object representing the source directory to remove a reference to that file. I want to add a reference to the destination directory to add a reference to this file and I want to update the file's metadata or what you would think of as an inode to update the C time on the file to show that it changed the directories and perhaps the M time on the destination directory
cues.zh: 我想修改表示源目录的对象，移除对该文件的引用。我想给目标目录添加一个引用，让它引用这个文件；我还想更新文件的元数据——你可以把它想成 inode——更新文件的 ctime，表明它更改了所在目录，也许还要更新目标目录的 mtime

cues.en: as well. And then close this transaction and now in a semantically rich way, I've described exactly what it is I'm trying to do. I'm trying to do these updates, which is renaming a file from one directory to another. And the DMU then takes this transaction,
cues.zh: 以及目标目录的 mtime。然后关闭这个事务。现在，我以一种语义丰富的方式，准确描述了我想要做什么。我要做这些更新，也就是把一个文件从一个目录重命名到另一个目录。然后 DMU 接收这个事务，

cues.en: bundles it together with any other transactions happening concurrently in time
cues.zh: 把它与时间上并发发生的其他事务打包在一起

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 并且

cues.en: bundles them up into a group that in a fit of creativity we call a transaction group.
cues.zh: 把它们打包成一个组，我们灵机一动，把它叫作事务组。

cues.en: And what this does is it describes a whole set of work that moves the final system from one consistent state to the next.
cues.zh: 它所做的，是描述一整套工作，把最终系统从一个一致状态推进到下一个一致状态。

cues.en: And it bundles these up, sends it down to the spa, which is not a nice relaxing place to be, but it's the storage pool allocator.
cues.zh: 它把这些打包起来，送到 SPA，这可不是什么轻松的休闲之地，而是存储池分配器。

cues.en: And now what the SPA has sitting in its hand
cues.zh: 现在 SPA 手里掌握的

cues.en: is a very semantically rich description of what it is that it needs to do. All the transactional information and in fact, a complete IO dependency graph that the DMU provides that says, before you modify this, you have to modify this other thing and this other thing in order to maintain consistency.
cues.zh: 是对它需要做什么的语义非常丰富的描述。所有事务信息，事实上，还有一个完整的 IO 依赖图，由 DMU 提供，它说：在你修改这个之前，你必须修改那个和另一个，以保持一致性。

cues.en: So the SPA, unlike the discs or the volume manager, doesn't have to scratch his head and say,
cues.zh: 所以 SPA 不像磁盘或卷管理器那样，不需要挠头琢磨说，

cues.en: I wonder if it'd be okay to reorder these two rights. No, it has the explicit information
cues.zh: 我想知道重新排序这两个写入是否可行。不，它手上有明确的信息

cues.en: in hand to know whether that's a legal transformation or not.
cues.zh: 来判断这是否是一个合法的转换。

cues.en: And then the SPA is what handles all the
cues.zh: 然后 SPA 负责处理所有

cues.en: grunt work, if you will, of dealing with physical storage devices. How to schedule the data, where to allocate it, how to do compression and encryption and check summing
cues.zh: 处理物理存储设备的繁琐工作，如果你愿意这么说的话。如何调度数据、在哪里分配、如何做压缩和加密以及校验和

cues.en: and all of these things. How to do the RAID algorithms, how to schedule the heads on the disks, all of this is what's handled in the SPA.
cues.zh: 以及所有这些事情。如何执行 RAID 算法、如何调度磁盘上的磁头，所有这些都在 SPA 中处理。

cues.en: And because everything is copy on right because of the way the DME and the SPA work together,
cues.zh: 而且因为一切都是写时复制，因为 DME 和 SPA 协同工作的方式，

cues.en: there's no resync of powers lost. We never overwrite live data so that if something goes wrong, just like in a database, you can sort of roll back to the previous version if you like.
cues.zh: 断电后不需要重新同步。我们从不覆盖活跃数据，所以如果出问题，就像在数据库中一样，你可以回滚到之前的版本，如果你愿意的话。

cues.en: And because of this, the SPA has all the information it needs in hand to do a much more optimal job of scheduling and
cues.zh: 正因如此，SPA 手中掌握了所需的所有信息，能更优化地调度和

cues.en: running the disk. So it runs at very high speeds most of the time.
cues.zh: 运行磁盘。所以大多数时候它以极高速度运转。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: the third
cues.zh: 第三

cues.en: major point about the architecture of ZFS is that it's designed fundamentally to provide universal
cues.zh:
ZFS 架构的一个核心要点是，它从根本上就是为了提供通用的
@@

cues.en: storage. That is to say that the data that you put in a storage pool doesn't have to be thought of as POSIX files or as blocks or as any one thing in particular.
cues.zh: 存储。也就是说，你放入存储池的数据不必被看作是 POSIX 文件、块设备或任何特定的单一对象。

cues.en: But rather, we have
cues.zh: 但相反，我们有

cues.en: up to two to the 48
cues.zh: 最高可达 2 的 48 次方

cues.en: datasets, and a dataset is just a collection of up to two to the 48 objects, each of which is up to two to 64 bytes in size. So each dataset is just a flat
cues.zh: 数据集，而数据集就是最多 2 的 48 次方个对象的集合，每个对象最大 2 的 64 次方字节。所以每个数据集就是一个扁平

cues.en: object store that's transactional.
cues.zh: 事务型对象存储。

cues.zh: 有了这个对象存储，你可以在上面放各种东西。可以放 POSIX 文件系统，可以直接在上面放 PNS，也可以在 POSIX 文件系统上放网络协议，

cues.en: and you can also just create a sort of degenerate simplest case of a dataset, which is a dataset that contains exactly one object
cues.zh: 你还可以建一个退化的最简单数据集，也就是只包含一个对象的数据集

cues.en: whose
cues.zh: 谁的

cues.en: contents are interpreted to be of the contents of a of a block device. So given our volume inhalation,
cues.zh: 内容被解释为块设备的内容。所以考虑到我们的卷初始化，

cues.zh: 然后你可以接上

cues.en: top of that or just provide access to raw storage. If you're using open Solaris, you've probably seen that we have roof on ZFS now. And we also have swap
cues.zh: 除此之外，或者只是提供对原始存储的访问。如果你在使用 open Solaris，你可能已经看到我们现在在 ZFS 上有了 roof。而且我们还有 swap。

cues.en: and dump devices just coming out of the storage pool as well. And you can even do things like putting your good old friend UFS
cues.zh: 而且转储设备也会刚刚从存储池中被释放出来。你甚至可以做一些事情，比如用上你的老朋友 UFS

cues.en: on top of ZFS, which might sound sound like a strange thing to do, but it actually turned out to be somewhat useful
cues.zh: 在ZFS之上，这听起来可能有点奇怪，但事实证明还挺有用的。

cues.en: in some of the
cues.zh: 在一些

cues.en: step Only two steps.
cues.zh: 只需两步。

cues.zh: 实际上在开发 UFS 的某些扩展时，我们在做的一些测试中，它证明确实有点用。

cues.en: So in the early days of of ZFS development,
cues.zh: 所以在 ZFS 开发的早期，

cues.en: UFS was limited to one terabyte and the UFS team wanted to grow that to 16.
cues.zh: UFS 限制在一太字节，而 UFS 团队希望把它扩展到 16 太字节。

cues.zh: 当然，涉及的代码改动相当简单，但测试并不简单，因为在当时，16 太字节的存储是非常巨大的。但我们能够做到的是，说没关系。你其实不需要 16 太字节的真实存储。你只需要 16 太字节的精简配置虚拟存储，

cues.zh: 结果证明，

cues.zh: 开启了压缩功能后，

cues.zh: 你可以在一个 ZFS 卷之上构建一个 UFS 文件系统，它消耗的空间大约是，我想，18 GB。所以几个

cues.en: Seagate,
cues.zh: 希捷 (Seagate)，

cues.zh: 这些快照中的每一个

cues.zh: 这些块指针所指向的块，本来会被释放掉

cues.zh: 所以当我们覆写这个区块时，比如在第40个时间点，

cues.zh: 我们的做法是这样：我们会说，你知道吗，这个内存块本来应该已经释放了

cues.en: but this guy is referencing him. So hanging off this snapshot, we say, yep, this block would have been freed, put him on the dead list. So if we ever go and delete this snapshot, we know
cues.zh: 但这家伙正在引用他。所以挂在这个快照上，我们说，是的，这个块本来应该被释放的，把它放到死亡列表中。所以如果我们去删除这个快照，我们就知道以后再也不用担心了

cues.en: that this block now should be added to the free map. And just in case you're wondering this in your mind as we're thinking about this,
cues.zh: 这个块现在应该被加入空闲映射表。以防你心里也在琢磨这件事——在我们思考这个问题的时候，

cues.en: a block only ever appears on one dead list. So we don't end up in an o of n situation simply because multiple snapshots reference a block, but rather the most recent snapshot that references the block is the one that contains it on the dead list. Yep.
cues.zh: 一个块只会出现在一个死亡列表里。所以，不会仅仅因为多个快照引用了同一个块，就出现 O(n) 的情况；引用它的最新快照才会把它放在自己的死亡列表里。对。

cues.en: And so then what happens is that deleting a snapshot is very simple. You screen down this dead list doing freeze for everything on it, poof you're done.

cues.zh: 所以我们在这个块树中

cues.en: block tree are blocks that have changed
cues.zh: 唯一需要搜索的

cues.en: since time twenty five.

cues.zh: 所以我们从顶部开始，问：37 大于 25 吗？

Go down the left. Is the time 37 greater than time, 25? Yes, it is. So now we send this block. Recurse back up. Is time 25 greater than time 25?
cues.zh: 是的，大于。因此，肯定有工作要做。进入下一层。我只做一个左侧深度优先搜索。时刻 37 大于时刻 25 吗？是的，大于。这个块需要发送。向左走。时刻 37 大于时刻 25 吗？是的，大于。所以现在我们发送这个块。递归返回上一层。时刻 25 大于时刻 25 吗？

cues.en: Why no, it isn't. So we know that this entire subtree,
cues.zh: 怎么会，并不大于。所以我们知道这个整棵子树——

cues.en: Go back up. Is 19 greater than 25?

cues.zh: 不，不大于。因此我们知道整棵子树都不需要遍历，因为无论我们在子树的什么地方修改一个块，

cues.en: so that any indirect block is as new as the youngest child underneath it. So we know nothing in this subtree has changed since time, in this case 19,
cues.zh: 以便任何间接块都与其下方最年轻的子代一样新。所以我们知道这棵子树中的任何内容自——这里是时刻 19——以来都没有改变过，

cues.en: and therefore nothing down here needs to be even visited. And now we're back up at the top. So the only blocks we wound up visiting are blocks that are actually part of the delta between time 25 and time 37.
cues.zh: 因此这里的任何内容甚至都不需要访问。现在我们回到了顶部。所以我们最终访问的唯一块，其实是时刻 25 到时刻 37 之间的增量部分。

cues.en: The other cool thing about it is that whereas if you're doing a bitmap based comparison, you end up generating a block level delta, in other words, a physical delta between the snapshots.
cues.zh: 关于它的另一个酷炫之处在于，如果你使用的是基于位图的比较，最终会生成一个块级别的增量，换句话说，也就是快照之间的物理增量。

cues.en: We end up doing over here is we don't actually send the uber block or the indirect blocks. We only actually send over the wire the modified data blocks. And because we have the structure of the file system in hand, because we're traversing it through its tree structure,
cues.zh: 我们在这里最终做的是：并不实际发送 uber block 或间接块。我们实际上只通过网络发送修改过的数据块。而且因为我们手头有文件系统的结构，因为我们是沿着它的树结构遍历，

cues.en: We actually send this over not as here's block number 92,
cues.zh: 我们其实不是以“这是第92个区块”的方式发送的，

cues.en: but as here is the contents of file foo at offset blah for size eight k or whatever the size happens to be. So we're sending a
cues.zh: 而是像这样：这是文件 foo 在某个偏移量处、大小为 8k（或者不管多大）的内容。所以我们发送的是一个

cues.en: semantic
cues.zh: 语义

cues.en: object delta. It's saying these are the objects
cues.zh: 对象 delta。它是在说这些是对象

cues.en: that changed and these are the regions within those objects that changed, which means that you can be sending from one system to a completely different system with a different RAID structure and a different,
cues.zh: 而变化的部分是这些对象内发生变化的区域，这意味着你可以从一个系统发送到一个完全不同的系统，其RAID结构不同，并且……

cues.en: you name it on the other end and
cues.zh: 另一端也是应有尽有，而且

cues.en: still successfully apply those changes. It's really just like Rsync
cues.zh: 依然能成功应用这些改动。这其实就像 Rsync 一样

cues.en: in that sense, except that when you're doing Rsync,
cues.zh: 在这个意义上，只不过当你用 Rsync 的时候，

cues.en: it has to do...
cues.zh: 它必须做……

cues.en: It doesn't get the advantage of being able to do the prune traversal. Right? If you ever use rsync, what it does,
cues.zh: 这样就没法利用剪枝遍历的优势了，对吧？如果你用过 rsync，就知道它会……

cues.zh: 通常，如果你有大量的数据需要从一个地方发送到另一个地方，它会花上好几个小时

cues.en: comparing the two trees on the source and destination systems coming up with the delta that says what changed, right, based on hash signatures of these things. And then it'll spend maybe five minutes transmitting what actually changed because it's typically not that much. So in other words, what happens is when you have large amounts of data that you're maintaining with rsync,
cues.zh: 比较源系统和目标系统上的两棵树，得出表示变化内容的差异，对吧，基于这些对象的哈希签名。然后它可能花大约五分钟传输实际变化的部分，因为通常变化没那么大。换句话说，当你有大量数据用 rsync 维护时，

cues.en: through the tree because it's looking at it as a file system tree. And of course, when you are looking at a tree of,

cues.zh: 所以我可以像刚才例子那样，生成 37 和 25 之间的差异。我也可以生成 37 和 19 之间的差异，
